title: Republic Day
whyCelebrated: Marks the day in 1950 when the Constitution of India came into effect, replacing the Government of India Act 1935 and establishing India as a sovereign democratic republic.
howCelebrated: A grand parade is held on Kartavya Path in New Delhi featuring the armed forces, tableaux from states and ministries, cultural performances and a flypast. The President takes the salute. Flag hoisting and parades occur across the country.
imageQuery: Republic Day India parade Kartavya Path

title: Independence Day
whyCelebrated: Commemorates India's independence from British colonial rule in 1947, ending nearly two centuries of British presence in the subcontinent.
howCelebrated: The Prime Minister hoists the national flag at the Red Fort in Delhi and addresses the nation. Flag-hoisting ceremonies, patriotic programmes and cultural events are held in schools, offices and public spaces nationwide.
imageQuery: Independence Day India Red Fort flag hoisting

title: Gandhi Jayanti
whyCelebrated: Celebrates the birth anniversary of Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi, leader of the Indian independence movement and proponent of non-violence. Observed globally as the International Day of Non-Violence.
howCelebrated: Prayer meetings and tributes are held at Raj Ghat in Delhi. Across the country there are cleanliness drives, community service, spinning demonstrations and singing of Gandhi's favourite bhajans.

title: National Youth Day
whyCelebrated: Marks the birth anniversary of Swami Vivekananda, celebrated to inspire the youth of India with his ideals and philosophy.
howCelebrated: Youth conventions, seminars, sports and cultural competitions are organised in schools, colleges and by youth organisations across the country.

title: Army Day
whyCelebrated: Commemorates the day in 1949 when Field Marshal K. M. Cariappa took over as the first Indian Commander-in-Chief of the Indian Army from the last British commander.
howCelebrated: Military parades and award ceremonies are held, with the main event in Delhi. The Army honours soldiers and showcases its capabilities.

title: National Voters' Day
whyCelebrated: Observed to mark the foundation day of the Election Commission of India (1950) and to encourage citizens, especially new voters, to participate in the democratic process.
howCelebrated: New voters are felicitated and issued voter ID cards; awareness programmes promote electoral participation.

title: National Science Day
whyCelebrated: Commemorates the discovery of the Raman Effect by Sir C. V. Raman in 1928, for which he received the Nobel Prize in Physics.
howCelebrated: Science exhibitions, lectures, quizzes and demonstrations are held in schools, colleges and research institutions to popularise science.

title: Ambedkar Jayanti
whyCelebrated: Celebrates the birth anniversary of Dr B. R. Ambedkar, principal architect of the Indian Constitution and a champion of social justice and the rights of marginalised communities.
howCelebrated: Processions, public lectures and tributes are held at statues and memorials. Many communities organise cultural and educational programmes.

title: Labour Day
whyCelebrated: International Workers' Day, observed to honour the contributions of workers and the labour movement and to advocate for workers' rights.
howCelebrated: Trade unions hold rallies and meetings. In Maharashtra and Gujarat the day coincides with state foundation days.

title: International Day of Yoga
whyCelebrated: Declared by the United Nations in 2014 on India's proposal, it celebrates yoga as a holistic practice for physical, mental and spiritual wellbeing.
howCelebrated: Mass yoga sessions are organised in public spaces, parks and institutions across India and the world, led by government and yoga organisations.

title: National Doctors' Day
whyCelebrated: Honours the birth and death anniversary of Dr B. C. Roy, eminent physician and former Chief Minister of West Bengal, recognising the contribution of doctors.
howCelebrated: Hospitals and medical bodies felicitate doctors and organise health camps and awareness programmes.

title: Kargil Vijay Diwas
whyCelebrated: Commemorates India's victory in the 1999 Kargil War against intrusions in the Kargil sector of Jammu and Kashmir.
howCelebrated: Wreath-laying ceremonies and tributes are held at war memorials, notably the Kargil War Memorial in Dras, honouring fallen soldiers.
imageQuery: Kargil Vijay Diwas war memorial Dras

title: National Sports Day
whyCelebrated: Marks the birth anniversary of hockey legend Major Dhyan Chand, celebrating sportsmanship and promoting fitness.
howCelebrated: Sports events, tournaments and the conferral of national sports awards take place; fitness drives are promoted nationwide.

title: Teachers' Day
whyCelebrated: Celebrates the birth anniversary of Dr Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, philosopher, statesman and the second President of India, honouring teachers.
howCelebrated: Students organise programmes and felicitate teachers; national awards for outstanding teachers are conferred.

title: Hindi Diwas
whyCelebrated: Marks the day in 1949 when Hindi in the Devanagari script was adopted as an official language of the Union of India.
howCelebrated: Government offices and educational institutions hold seminars, competitions and award ceremonies promoting Hindi.

title: Engineer's Day
whyCelebrated: Honours the birth anniversary of Sir M. Visvesvaraya, eminent engineer and statesman, recognising the contribution of engineers to nation-building.
howCelebrated: Engineering institutions and bodies hold technical seminars, exhibitions and felicitations.

title: Indian Air Force Day
whyCelebrated: Commemorates the official establishment of the Indian Air Force in 1932.
howCelebrated: Air displays, parades and ceremonies are held, with a major event and flypast at an air force station.

title: Rashtriya Ekta Diwas
whyCelebrated: National Unity Day marks the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, who integrated the princely states into the Indian Union.
howCelebrated: The 'Run for Unity', pledges and tributes are organised; the Statue of Unity in Gujarat is a focal point of celebrations.
imageQuery: Statue of Unity Sardar Patel Rashtriya Ekta Diwas

title: National Education Day
whyCelebrated: Marks the birth anniversary of Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, independent India's first Education Minister, celebrating his contribution to education.
howCelebrated: Schools and colleges hold seminars, essay competitions and awareness drives on the value of education.

title: Children's Day
whyCelebrated: Celebrated on the birth anniversary of Jawaharlal Nehru, India's first Prime Minister, who was fond of children and known as 'Chacha Nehru'.
howCelebrated: Schools organise games, cultural programmes and special activities for children.

title: Constitution Day
whyCelebrated: Samvidhan Diwas commemorates the adoption of the Constitution of India by the Constituent Assembly in 1949.
howCelebrated: Readings of the Preamble, lectures and educational programmes on constitutional values are held in institutions nationwide.

title: Indian Navy Day
whyCelebrated: Commemorates Operation Trident, a naval strike on Karachi harbour during the 1971 Indo-Pak war.
howCelebrated: Naval ship visits, operational demonstrations and ceremonies are held, with public displays at coastal cities.

title: Uttar Pradesh Day (UP Diwas)
whyCelebrated: Commemorates the formation of the state of Uttar Pradesh in its present name in 1950.
howCelebrated: State-organised cultural programmes, exhibitions of local crafts and industries, and felicitations are held across the state.

title: Manipur Statehood Day
whyCelebrated: Marks Manipur attaining full statehood in 1972 under the North-Eastern Areas (Reorganisation) Act 1971.
howCelebrated: Official functions, cultural performances and parades are held in Imphal and across the state.

title: Meghalaya Statehood Day
whyCelebrated: Marks Meghalaya attaining full statehood in 1972, carved out of Assam.
howCelebrated: Government functions and cultural events celebrating Khasi, Garo and Jaintia heritage are held.

title: Tripura Statehood Day
whyCelebrated: Marks Tripura attaining full statehood in 1972 under the North-Eastern Areas (Reorganisation) Act.
howCelebrated: Official ceremonies and cultural performances showcasing tribal and Bengali heritage are held in Agartala.

title: Himachal Day (Full Statehood)
whyCelebrated: Commemorates Himachal Pradesh becoming the 18th full state of India in 1971.
howCelebrated: State functions, cultural programmes and award ceremonies are held in Shimla and district headquarters.

title: Rajasthan Day (Rajasthan Diwas)
whyCelebrated: Marks the unification of princely states into the state of Rajasthan in 1949.
howCelebrated: Cultural festivals, folk performances, exhibitions and heritage walks are organised across Jaipur and other cities.

title: Bihar Day (Bihar Diwas)
whyCelebrated: Commemorates the carving out of Bihar as a separate province from the Bengal Presidency in 1912.
howCelebrated: Three-day celebrations with cultural shows, exhibitions and concerts are held in Patna and at Bihar centres elsewhere.

title: Utkala Dibasa (Odisha Day)
whyCelebrated: Marks the formation of Odisha as a separate province on linguistic basis in 1936.
howCelebrated: Cultural programmes, processions and tributes to Odia language and pride are held across the state.
imageQuery: Utkala Dibasa Odisha Day Odia culture

title: Himachal Day
whyCelebrated: Commemorates the formation of Himachal Pradesh as a Part-C state in 1948 by integrating hill principalities.
howCelebrated: Official functions and cultural programmes are held; observed alongside the state's hill heritage.

title: Maharashtra Day (Maharashtra Din)
whyCelebrated: Marks the formation of the state of Maharashtra in 1960 when the Bombay State was split on linguistic lines.
howCelebrated: Parades, cultural programmes and official functions are held; the main ceremony takes place in Mumbai.

title: Gujarat Day (Gujarat Sthapana Divas)
whyCelebrated: Marks the formation of the state of Gujarat in 1960 when the bilingual Bombay State was divided.
howCelebrated: Cultural events, exhibitions and official ceremonies celebrating Gujarati heritage are held statewide.

title: Sikkim Statehood Day
whyCelebrated: Commemorates Sikkim becoming the 22nd state of India in 1975.
howCelebrated: Official ceremonies and cultural performances are held in Gangtok and across the state.

title: Telangana Formation Day
whyCelebrated: Marks the formation of Telangana as India's 29th state in 2014, carved out of Andhra Pradesh.
howCelebrated: State-wide celebrations with cultural programmes, illuminations and official functions are held in Hyderabad.

title: Jharkhand Foundation Day
whyCelebrated: Marks the creation of Jharkhand as a separate state in 2000, carved out of Bihar. Coincides with the birth anniversary of tribal icon Birsa Munda.
howCelebrated: Cultural programmes celebrating tribal heritage, tributes to Birsa Munda, and official functions are held.

title: Uttarakhand Foundation Day
whyCelebrated: Marks the creation of Uttarakhand (initially Uttaranchal) as a separate state in 2000, carved out of Uttar Pradesh.
howCelebrated: Official functions and cultural programmes celebrating Garhwali and Kumaoni heritage are held in Dehradun.

title: Nagaland Foundation Day
whyCelebrated: Commemorates Nagaland becoming the 16th state of India in 1963.
howCelebrated: Cultural events and official ceremonies are held; the period coincides with the famed Hornbill Festival.

title: Karnataka Rajyotsava (Kannada Rajyotsava)
whyCelebrated: Marks the formation of Karnataka state in 1956, unifying Kannada-speaking regions. The state was renamed from Mysore to Karnataka in 1973.
howCelebrated: The red-and-yellow Kannada flag is hoisted, Rajyotsava awards are conferred, and cultural processions and programmes are held across the state.

title: Andhra Pradesh Formation Day
whyCelebrated: Marks the formation of Andhra Pradesh in 1956 by merging Telugu-speaking areas. Observed as the state's formation day.
howCelebrated: Cultural programmes and official functions celebrating Telugu heritage are held.
imageQuery: Andhra Pradesh Formation Day Telugu culture

title: Kerala Piravi (Kerala Day)
whyCelebrated: Marks the formation of Kerala state in 1956 by unifying Malayalam-speaking regions of Travancore, Cochin and Malabar.
howCelebrated: Cultural programmes, exhibitions and events celebrating Malayalam language and Kerala's heritage are held statewide.

title: Madhya Pradesh Foundation Day (MP Sthapana Diwas)
whyCelebrated: Marks the formation of Madhya Pradesh in 1956 under the States Reorganisation Act.
howCelebrated: Week-long cultural festivities, performances and exhibitions are organised, with major events in Bhopal.

title: Chhattisgarh Foundation Day (Rajyotsava)
whyCelebrated: Marks the creation of Chhattisgarh as a separate state in 2000, carved out of Madhya Pradesh.
howCelebrated: The multi-day Rajyotsava features folk performances, craft exhibitions and cultural programmes in Raipur.

title: Haryana Day (Haryana Diwas)
whyCelebrated: Marks the formation of Haryana as a separate state in 1966, carved out of Punjab on linguistic lines.
howCelebrated: Official functions, cultural programmes and award ceremonies are held across the state.

title: Punjab Day (Punjab Diwas)
whyCelebrated: Associated with the reorganisation of Punjab in 1966 when Haryana and parts of Himachal were separated.
howCelebrated: Cultural events and official functions celebrating Punjabi heritage are held.

title: Asom Divas (Sukapha Divas)
whyCelebrated: Asom Divas commemorates the arrival of Ahom king Chaolung Sukapha in the Brahmaputra valley in the 13th century, marking the foundation of the Ahom kingdom. It is observed as Assam Day, though Assam has no single modern statehood date.
howCelebrated: Cultural programmes, tributes to Sukapha and events celebrating Assamese identity are held.

title: Goa Statehood Day
whyCelebrated: Marks Goa attaining full statehood in 1987, having earlier been part of the Union Territory of Goa, Daman and Diu.
howCelebrated: Official functions and cultural programmes are held across the state.

title: Tamil Nadu Day
whyCelebrated: Associated with the formation of the linguistic state in 1956; the state was renamed from Madras to Tamil Nadu in 1969. Observance of a single 'foundation day' is not uniformly standardised.
howCelebrated: Cultural events celebrating Tamil language and heritage are held where observed.

title: Arunachal Pradesh Statehood Day
whyCelebrated: Marks Arunachal Pradesh attaining full statehood in 1987.
howCelebrated: Official ceremonies and tribal cultural performances are held in Itanagar and across districts.

title: Mizoram Statehood Day
whyCelebrated: Marks Mizoram attaining full statehood in 1987 under the State of Mizoram Act 1986.
howCelebrated: Official functions and Mizo cultural programmes are held in Aizawl.

title: West Bengal Foundation Day (Paschim Banga Divas)
whyCelebrated: A foundation day for West Bengal observed on 20 April has been promoted by the Raj Bhavan, but the date is politically contested and not universally accepted by the state government.
howCelebrated: Where observed, official and cultural functions are held; the observance remains a subject of debate.

title: Puducherry De Facto Transfer Day
whyCelebrated: Marks the de facto transfer of the French establishments of Puducherry to India in 1954. Full legal transfer (de jure) occurred in 1962.
howCelebrated: Official functions and cultural programmes reflecting the region's Franco-Tamil heritage are held.

title: Chandigarh Formation
whyCelebrated: Chandigarh was constituted as a Union Territory in 1966 when Haryana was carved out of Punjab; the city serves as the shared capital of both states.
howCelebrated: Civic and cultural events are held in the planned city designed by Le Corbusier.

title: Lakshadweep Formation Day
whyCelebrated: Lakshadweep was constituted as a Union Territory in 1956 (renamed from Laccadive, Minicoy and Amindivi Islands in 1973).
howCelebrated: Local cultural and civic events are held across the islands.

title: Jammu & Kashmir UT Formation
whyCelebrated: Marks the reorganisation of the former state of Jammu and Kashmir into a Union Territory in 2019.
howCelebrated: Administrative observance; cultural significance varies locally.

title: Ladakh UT Formation
whyCelebrated: Marks the creation of Ladakh as a separate Union Territory in 2019 following the reorganisation of Jammu and Kashmir.
howCelebrated: Administrative observance; local cultural events vary.

title: Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu Merger
state: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
whyCelebrated: The two former union territories were merged into a single Union Territory in 2020.
howCelebrated: Administrative observance; local civic events vary.

title: Delhi (NCT) Establishment
whyCelebrated: The National Capital Territory of Delhi with a legislative assembly was established under the 69th Constitutional Amendment, effective 1992.
howCelebrated: Administrative observance; not widely marked as a public celebration.

title: Andaman & Nicobar Islands
whyCelebrated: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands have been administered as a Union Territory of India since 1956.
howCelebrated: Local cultural and civic events are held; the islands are also noted for the Cellular Jail National Memorial.

title: Diwali (Deepavali)
whyCelebrated: The festival of lights celebrates the victory of light over darkness and good over evil. It commemorates Lord Rama's return to Ayodhya after defeating Ravana, and is also associated with the worship of Goddess Lakshmi for prosperity.
howCelebrated: Homes are cleaned and decorated with diyas, candles and rangoli. People light fireworks, exchange sweets and gifts, perform Lakshmi puja, and wear new clothes. It is celebrated over five days in many regions.
imageQuery: Diwali festival lights diya rangoli celebration

title: Holi
whyCelebrated: The festival of colours marks the arrival of spring and the triumph of good over evil, celebrating the legend of Holika and Prahlad, and the playful love of Radha and Krishna.
howCelebrated: People smear and throw coloured powders (gulal) and water at each other, sing and dance to music, and gather for community feasts. The night before, Holika bonfires are lit.
imageQuery: Holi festival colours gulal celebration India

title: Dussehra (Vijayadashami)
whyCelebrated: Marks the victory of Lord Rama over the demon king Ravana, and of Goddess Durga over the buffalo demon Mahishasura, symbolising the triumph of good over evil.
howCelebrated: Effigies of Ravana, Meghnad and Kumbhakarna are burnt amid fireworks. Ramlila plays are staged, and in some regions it concludes Navratri and Durga Puja celebrations.

title: Durga Puja
whyCelebrated: Celebrates the victory of Goddess Durga over the demon Mahishasura, honouring the divine feminine power (Shakti). It is the most important festival of the Bengali calendar.
howCelebrated: Elaborately crafted pandals house idols of Durga. Devotees offer prayers, dhunuchi dance and pushpanjali; the festival culminates in immersion (visarjan) of idols accompanied by sindoor khela.

title: Ganesh Chaturthi
whyCelebrated: Celebrates the birth of Lord Ganesha, the remover of obstacles and god of wisdom and new beginnings.
howCelebrated: Clay idols of Ganesha are installed in homes and public pandals, worshipped for one to eleven days with prayers and modak offerings, then immersed in water in grand processions.

title: Navratri
whyCelebrated: A nine-night festival honouring the nine forms of Goddess Durga, celebrating divine feminine energy. Observed differently across regions, it precedes Dussehra.
howCelebrated: Devotees fast, worship the goddess and perform Garba and Dandiya dances, especially in Gujarat. In the south, Golu doll displays are arranged.

title: Krishna Janmashtami
whyCelebrated: Celebrates the birth of Lord Krishna, the eighth avatar of Vishnu, revered for his teachings in the Bhagavad Gita.
howCelebrated: Devotees fast until midnight (Krishna's birth time), sing bhajans, and decorate temples. In Maharashtra, Dahi Handi human pyramids break pots of curd.

title: Ram Navami
whyCelebrated: Celebrates the birth of Lord Rama, the seventh avatar of Vishnu and hero of the Ramayana.
howCelebrated: Devotees visit temples, recite the Ramayana, observe fasts and take out processions. Ayodhya, Rama's birthplace, sees major celebrations.

title: Maha Shivaratri
whyCelebrated: The great night of Shiva commemorates the cosmic union of Shiva and Parvati and is dedicated to the worship of Lord Shiva.
howCelebrated: Devotees observe night-long vigils and fasts, offer milk and bilva leaves to the Shiva lingam, and chant 'Om Namah Shivaya' at temples.
imageQuery: Maha Shivaratri temple Shiva lingam abhishekam

title: Raksha Bandhan
whyCelebrated: Celebrates the bond between brothers and sisters; the sister ties a protective thread (rakhi) and the brother vows to protect her.
howCelebrated: Sisters tie rakhis on brothers' wrists, apply tilak and exchange sweets and gifts amid family gatherings.

title: Makar Sankranti
whyCelebrated: Marks the sun's transition into Capricorn (Makara) and the start of longer days; a harvest festival celebrated under many regional names.
howCelebrated: People fly kites, take holy dips in rivers, prepare sesame and jaggery sweets, and light bonfires. Regional forms include Pongal, Lohri, Uttarayan and Bihu.

title: Guru Nanak Jayanti (Gurpurab)
whyCelebrated: Celebrates the birth anniversary of Guru Nanak Dev, the founder of Sikhism and the first of the ten Sikh Gurus.
howCelebrated: Gurdwaras hold Akhand Path (continuous reading of the Guru Granth Sahib), Nagar Kirtan processions, langar (community meals) and devotional singing.
imageQuery: Guru Nanak Jayanti Nagar Kirtan gurdwara

title: Mahavir Jayanti
whyCelebrated: Celebrates the birth of Lord Mahavira, the 24th and last Tirthankara of Jainism, who taught non-violence, truth and non-attachment.
howCelebrated: Jains visit temples, take out processions of Mahavira's idol, perform charitable acts and meditate on his teachings.

title: Buddha Purnima (Vesak)
whyCelebrated: Commemorates the birth, enlightenment and death (parinirvana) of Gautama Buddha, the founder of Buddhism.
howCelebrated: Devotees visit monasteries, offer prayers and flowers, meditate, and engage in acts of charity and kindness. Bodhi trees are venerated.

title: Eid al-Fitr
whyCelebrated: Marks the end of Ramadan, the holy month of fasting, and is a celebration of gratitude and breaking the fast.
howCelebrated: Muslims offer special congregational prayers (Eid namaz), wear new clothes, give Zakat (charity), and share festive meals with family and community.

title: Eid al-Adha (Bakrid)
whyCelebrated: The festival of sacrifice commemorates Prophet Ibrahim's willingness to sacrifice his son in obedience to God; it coincides with the Hajj pilgrimage.
howCelebrated: Muslims offer prayers, perform the ritual sacrifice (Qurbani) of an animal, and distribute the meat among family, friends and the needy.

title: Muharram
whyCelebrated: Marks the start of the Islamic new year; the tenth day (Ashura) commemorates the martyrdom of Imam Hussain, the Prophet's grandson, at Karbala.
howCelebrated: Shia communities hold mourning processions with tazias, recitations (majlis) and acts of remembrance; many observe fasting and charity.

title: Christmas
whyCelebrated: Celebrates the birth of Jesus Christ, central to the Christian faith.
howCelebrated: Churches hold midnight mass and carol services. Homes and streets are decorated with lights, stars and nativity scenes; families exchange gifts and share festive meals.

title: Good Friday & Easter
whyCelebrated: Good Friday commemorates the crucifixion of Jesus Christ; Easter celebrates his resurrection, the cornerstone of Christian belief.
howCelebrated: Good Friday is observed with solemn church services and processions. Easter brings joyful masses, feasting, decorated eggs and family gatherings.

title: Chhath Puja
whyCelebrated: An ancient festival dedicated to the Sun God (Surya) and Chhathi Maiya, offering thanks for sustaining life and seeking blessings for family wellbeing.
howCelebrated: Devotees observe rigorous fasting, stand in water and offer arghya (offerings) to the setting and rising sun on riverbanks and ghats over four days.
imageQuery: Chhath Puja ghat sun offering Bihar

title: Vasant Panchami (Saraswati Puja)
whyCelebrated: Marks the onset of spring and is dedicated to Goddess Saraswati, deity of knowledge, music and arts.
howCelebrated: Devotees wear yellow, worship Saraswati, and initiate young children into learning (Vidyarambham). Educational institutions hold special pujas.

title: Onam
whyCelebrated: Kerala's harvest festival celebrating the homecoming of the legendary King Mahabali, symbolising prosperity and equality during his mythical reign.
howCelebrated: Homes are decorated with floral rangoli (pookalam), grand feasts (Sadya) are served on banana leaves, and snake-boat races, Pulikali tiger dances and folk performances are held.
imageQuery: Onam Kerala pookalam sadya boat race

title: Vishu
whyCelebrated: Marks the astronomical new year in Kerala and the sun's transit, celebrated for prosperity and new beginnings.
howCelebrated: The day begins with viewing the auspicious Vishukkani arrangement; elders give money (Vishukkaineetam) to the young, and families feast and burst crackers.

title: Thrissur Pooram
whyCelebrated: A spectacular temple festival in Thrissur known as the 'pooram of all poorams', celebrating the deities of surrounding temples.
howCelebrated: Caparisoned elephants are paraded with ornate parasols, accompanied by percussion ensembles (Panchavadyam) and a grand fireworks display.

title: Theyyam
whyCelebrated: A ritualistic dance-worship form of north Kerala in which performers embody deities and ancestral spirits.
howCelebrated: Performers in elaborate costumes, towering headgear and vivid face paint enter a trance and bless devotees at temple courtyards and sacred groves.

title: Pongal
whyCelebrated: A four-day harvest festival thanking the Sun God, nature and cattle for a bountiful harvest; the most important Tamil festival.
howCelebrated: The signature dish Pongal is cooked in new pots until it boils over (symbolising abundance). Cattle are honoured on Mattu Pongal, and homes are decorated with kolam.
imageQuery: Pongal Tamil Nadu pot kolam harvest

title: Thaipusam
whyCelebrated: Dedicated to Lord Murugan, commemorating the occasion when Goddess Parvati gave him a divine spear to vanquish evil.
howCelebrated: Devotees carry kavadi (ornate burdens), some piercing their bodies as acts of penance, and process to Murugan temples amid music and chanting.

title: Karthigai Deepam
whyCelebrated: An ancient festival of lights celebrating Lord Shiva; the great beacon atop Tiruvannamalai hill is its most famous expression.
howCelebrated: Rows of oil lamps illuminate homes, streets and temples. A massive cauldron of flame (Maha Deepam) is lit on Arunachala hill.

title: Mysuru Dasara
whyCelebrated: Karnataka's grand state festival (Nadahabba) celebrating the victory of Goddess Chamundeshwari over the demon Mahishasura.
howCelebrated: The illuminated Mysore Palace anchors ten days of festivities, culminating in the Jumboo Savari procession with a golden howdah on a caparisoned elephant.
imageQuery: Mysuru Dasara palace illumination elephant procession

title: Ugadi
whyCelebrated: The Telugu and Kannada New Year, marking the start of a new lunar year and the arrival of spring.
howCelebrated: Homes are cleaned and decorated with mango-leaf torans. The ritual Ugadi Pachadi, blending six tastes, symbolises life's varied experiences. Panchanga Sravanam (almanac reading) is heard.

title: Hampi Utsav (Vijaya Utsav)
whyCelebrated: A cultural festival celebrating the heritage of the Vijayanagara Empire amid the ruins of Hampi, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
howCelebrated: The historic site comes alive with light-and-sound shows, classical and folk dance, music concerts, processions and craft displays.
imageQuery: Hampi Utsav ruins light show Karnataka

title: Gudi Padwa
whyCelebrated: The Marathi New Year, marking the arrival of spring and, by tradition, the day Lord Brahma created the universe.
howCelebrated: A Gudi (a bright cloth with a garlanded pot) is hoisted outside homes for prosperity. Families draw rangoli, wear new clothes and prepare festive dishes.

title: Pandharpur Wari (Ashadhi Ekadashi)
whyCelebrated: A centuries-old pilgrimage of Varkari devotees to the Vithoba temple at Pandharpur, expressing devotion to Lord Vitthal.
howCelebrated: Pilgrims (warkaris) walk hundreds of kilometres carrying palkhis (palanquins) of saints, singing abhangs and chanting the name of Vitthal.

title: Nag Panchami
whyCelebrated: A festival venerating snakes (Nagas), seeking their blessings and protection from snakebite.
howCelebrated: Devotees offer milk and prayers to snake idols and live snakes, and worship at Naga temples; women pray for the wellbeing of their families.

title: Uttarayan (International Kite Festival)
whyCelebrated: Gujarat's celebration of Makar Sankranti, marking the sun's northward journey, famed for its skies full of kites.
howCelebrated: People take to rooftops to fly and battle colourful kites all day, calling 'kai po che' on cutting a rival's string; the festival draws international kite-flyers to Ahmedabad.

title: Rann Utsav
whyCelebrated: A months-long cultural festival celebrating the white salt desert of the Kutch under the full moon.
howCelebrated: Visitors stay in tent cities and enjoy folk music and dance, handicraft bazaars, camel rides and the surreal moonlit white Rann landscape.
imageQuery: Rann Utsav Kutch white desert tents

title: Dwarka Janmashtami
whyCelebrated: Krishna Janmashtami at Dwarka, the legendary kingdom of Lord Krishna, draws devotees to one of Hinduism's holiest sites.
howCelebrated: The Dwarkadhish temple holds special rituals, bhajans and midnight celebrations of Krishna's birth, with thousands of pilgrims attending.

title: Baisakhi (Vaisakhi)
whyCelebrated: A harvest festival and the Sikh new year; it also marks the founding of the Khalsa by Guru Gobind Singh in 1699.
howCelebrated: Farmers celebrate the wheat harvest with energetic Bhangra and Gidda dances. Gurdwaras hold special prayers, Nagar Kirtan processions and langar.

title: Lohri
whyCelebrated: A winter folk festival marking the end of the coldest days and the harvest of rabi crops; associated with the folk hero Dulla Bhatti.
howCelebrated: Bonfires are lit at night around which people sing, dance Bhangra and Gidda, and toss sesame, popcorn and jaggery into the flames.

title: Hola Mohalla
whyCelebrated: A Sikh festival established by Guru Gobind Singh as an occasion to display martial skills, held the day after Holi.
howCelebrated: Nihang Sikhs demonstrate Gatka (martial arts), horsemanship and mock battles at Anandpur Sahib, followed by kirtan, poetry and langar.
imageQuery: Hola Mohalla Nihang Gatka Anandpur Sahib

title: Pushkar Camel Fair
whyCelebrated: One of the world's largest camel and livestock fairs, held around the sacred Pushkar lake during Kartik Purnima.
howCelebrated: Traders gather with thousands of camels and cattle; the fair features camel races, folk music, competitions and a holy dip in Pushkar lake.

title: Desert Festival, Jaisalmer
whyCelebrated: A vibrant celebration of Rajasthani desert culture set against the golden dunes near Jaisalmer.
howCelebrated: The festival showcases folk dances, music, camel polo and races, turban-tying and moustache competitions, culminating in performances on the Sam sand dunes.
imageQuery: Jaisalmer Desert Festival camel dunes Rajasthan

title: Gangaur
whyCelebrated: A festival honouring Goddess Gauri (Parvati), celebrating marital love and devotion; especially important for women.
howCelebrated: Women dress in finery, worship clay idols of Gauri and Isar, and carry them in colourful processions with folk songs, particularly grand in Jaipur and Udaipur.

title: Teej
whyCelebrated: A monsoon festival celebrating the union of Shiva and Parvati, observed mainly by women for marital bliss and wellbeing.
howCelebrated: Women apply mehndi, wear green, swing on flower-decked swings, sing folk songs and observe fasts; Jaipur hosts a royal Teej procession.
imageQuery: Teej festival swing mehndi women Rajasthan

title: Poila Boishakh (Bengali New Year)
whyCelebrated: The Bengali New Year, marking the first day of the Bengali calendar and a time of fresh beginnings.
howCelebrated: Businesses open new account books (Halkhata), homes draw alpana, and people exchange greetings, visit temples and enjoy cultural programmes and feasts.
imageQuery: Poila Boishakh Bengali New Year Kolkata

title: Kali Puja
whyCelebrated: Dedicated to Goddess Kali, the fierce form of Shakti, celebrated on the new-moon night, coinciding with Diwali in Bengal.
howCelebrated: Idols of Kali are worshipped through the night with offerings, mantras and lamps; pandals and homes are illuminated and fireworks light the sky.

title: Jagaddhatri Puja
whyCelebrated: Honours Goddess Jagaddhatri, a form of Durga as the protector of the universe; especially grand in Chandannagar and Krishnanagar.
howCelebrated: Elaborate idols and pandals are set up, with renowned lighting displays in Chandannagar and a grand immersion procession.

title: Bihu (Bohag/Rongali Bihu)
whyCelebrated: Assam's most important festival, Rongali Bihu marks the Assamese New Year and the onset of the agricultural season.
howCelebrated: Young men and women perform the energetic Bihu dance to dhol and pepa, exchange gamosa, feast and celebrate over several days.

title: Ambubachi Mela
whyCelebrated: An annual fair at the Kamakhya Temple in Guwahati associated with the goddess's yearly cycle and the fertility of the earth.
howCelebrated: The temple closes for a few days then reopens; thousands of tantric sadhus and devotees gather for one of the most significant Shakti gatherings.

title: Me-Dam-Me-Phi
whyCelebrated: An ancestor-worship festival of the Ahom community, paying homage to departed forefathers and seeking their blessings.
howCelebrated: Families and communities make offerings to ancestors and a supreme god, reaffirming Ahom heritage and unity.

title: Rath Yatra (Puri)
whyCelebrated: The famous chariot festival of Lord Jagannath, Balabhadra and Subhadra at Puri, when the deities journey to the Gundicha Temple.
howCelebrated: Three towering wooden chariots are pulled by thousands of devotees along the Grand Road; pulling the ropes is considered deeply auspicious.

title: Raja Parba
whyCelebrated: A three-day festival celebrating womanhood and the earth's fertility, marking the onset of the monsoon.
howCelebrated: Women and girls rest from work, wear new clothes, play on decorated swings and enjoy folk games; the festival honours Mother Earth.

title: Konark Dance Festival
whyCelebrated: A classical dance festival set against the backdrop of the Sun Temple at Konark, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
howCelebrated: Leading exponents of Odissi, Bharatanatyam and other classical forms perform on an open-air stage near the iconic temple.
imageQuery: Konark Dance Festival Sun Temple Odissi

title: Sama Chakeva
whyCelebrated: A folk festival of the Mithila region celebrating the bond between brothers and sisters through bird-shaped clay figurines.
howCelebrated: Girls craft and decorate clay idols of Sama and Chakeva, sing folk songs, and perform rituals wishing for their brothers' wellbeing.
imageQuery: Sama Chakeva Mithila Bihar clay birds

title: Sonepur Cattle Fair
whyCelebrated: Asia's largest cattle fair, held at the confluence of the Ganga and Gandak around Kartik Purnima.
howCelebrated: Traders gather to buy and sell livestock including elephants and horses; the fair features a holy dip, folk performances and bustling bazaars.

title: Sarhul
whyCelebrated: A spring festival of the Adivasi communities of Jharkhand worshipping nature and the village deity, marking the new year.
howCelebrated: The sal tree is venerated; priests (pahan) perform rituals, and communities dance and sing to welcome the flowering season.
imageQuery: Sarhul Jharkhand tribal festival sal tree

title: Karma Parab
whyCelebrated: A tribal festival worshipping the Karam tree, symbolising youth, fertility and the bond with nature.
howCelebrated: A Karam branch is installed and worshipped; young people fast, sing and perform the Karma dance through the night.

title: Sohrai
whyCelebrated: A harvest and cattle festival of Jharkhand's tribal communities, famed for the distinctive Sohrai wall paintings.
howCelebrated: Homes are decorated with traditional Sohrai art, cattle are bathed, adorned and worshipped, and communities feast and dance.

title: Bastar Dussehra
whyCelebrated: A unique 75-day Dussehra in the Bastar region honouring the local goddess Danteshwari, distinct from the Rama-Ravana tradition.
howCelebrated: Tribal rituals, the building of a wooden chariot, and ceremonies involving local deities and communities mark this exceptionally long festival.

title: Hareli
whyCelebrated: Chhattisgarh's first major festival of the year, celebrating greenery and the farming season's start.
howCelebrated: Farmers worship agricultural tools and cattle, decorate homes with neem branches, and play traditional games like Gedi (stilt walking).

title: Bathukamma
whyCelebrated: A vibrant floral festival of Telangana celebrating womanhood and the goddess Gauri, marking the monsoon's bounty.
howCelebrated: Women arrange seasonal flowers in conical tiers, sing and dance around them in circles over nine days, then immerse them in water.
imageQuery: Bathukamma Telangana flower stack women dance

title: Bonalu
whyCelebrated: A folk festival of Telangana honouring Goddess Mahakali, offering thanks and seeking protection, especially in Hyderabad and Secunderabad.
howCelebrated: Women carry decorated pots (bonam) of rice, milk and jaggery on their heads to the temple; rituals include Pothuraju performances and trance dances.

title: Tirumala Brahmotsavam
whyCelebrated: The grandest annual festival at the Tirumala Venkateswara Temple, one of the world's most visited pilgrimage sites.
howCelebrated: Over nine days the deity is taken in procession on a series of ornate vahanams (mounts); the Garuda Seva day draws enormous crowds.

title: Goa Carnival
whyCelebrated: A pre-Lenten carnival of Portuguese origin, unique to Goa, filled with colour, music and revelry.
howCelebrated: King Momo presides over vibrant float parades, street dances, music and feasting across Panaji and other towns over several days.

title: Shigmo
whyCelebrated: Goa's spring festival, a Konkani celebration akin to Holi, marking the harvest and the return of warriors of yore.
howCelebrated: Colourful float parades depict mythological scenes, accompanied by traditional folk dances like Ghode Modni and Romta Mel.
imageQuery: Shigmo Goa float parade folk dance

title: Sao Joao (Feast of St John)
whyCelebrated: A monsoon festival honouring St John the Baptist, celebrated with exuberant water revelry.
howCelebrated: Young men wearing flower-and-leaf crowns leap into wells and ponds to celebrate; villages enjoy music, feni and boat festivities.
imageQuery: Sao Joao Goa well jumping flower crown

title: Kullu Dussehra
whyCelebrated: A week-long international festival in the Kullu valley that begins when Dussehra ends elsewhere, centred on Lord Raghunath.
howCelebrated: Hundreds of village deities are carried in palanquins to assemble before Lord Raghunath; processions, fairs and cultural shows fill the valley.

title: Minjar Mela
whyCelebrated: A historic fair in Chamba marking the maize-flowering season and a legendary victory, celebrated for over a millennium.
howCelebrated: People wear minjar (silk tassels symbolising maize shoots), and a week of processions, folk music and sports culminates in offerings to the river.

title: Losar
whyCelebrated: The Tibetan Buddhist New Year, celebrated in the Himalayan regions to welcome the new year and ward off evil spirits.
howCelebrated: Monasteries hold prayers and masked Cham dances; homes are cleaned and decorated, and families gather for feasts and rituals.
imageQuery: Losar Tibetan New Year Cham dance monastery

title: Dev Deepawali (Varanasi)
whyCelebrated: The 'Diwali of the Gods' in Varanasi, celebrated on Kartik Purnima fifteen days after Diwali.
howCelebrated: The ghats of the Ganga are lit with hundreds of thousands of earthen lamps; grand Ganga aarti, processions and floating diyas create a spectacular sight.
imageQuery: Dev Deepawali Varanasi ghats lamps Ganga

title: Lathmar Holi (Barsana)
whyCelebrated: A playful and famous form of Holi in Barsana and Nandgaon, re-enacting Krishna's legendary visits to Radha's village.
howCelebrated: Women playfully beat men with sticks (lath) while the men shield themselves, amid colours, folk songs and Braj traditions.

title: Taj Mahotsav
whyCelebrated: A ten-day cultural festival in Agra near the Taj Mahal showcasing India's arts, crafts and cuisine.
howCelebrated: Artisans from across the country display their crafts, with folk and classical performances, food stalls and a festive bazaar atmosphere.

title: Harela
whyCelebrated: A festival of the Kumaon region celebrating greenery, the monsoon and the start of the sowing season.
howCelebrated: Families sow seeds days in advance and harvest the young shoots (harela), placing them on the head as blessings for prosperity and good harvest.

title: Ganga Dussehra
whyCelebrated: Celebrates the descent (avataran) of the holy river Ganga from heaven to earth, honouring her sanctity.
howCelebrated: Devotees take ritual dips in the Ganga, perform aarti at ghats in Haridwar and Rishikesh, and offer prayers for purification.

title: Nanda Devi Raj Jat
whyCelebrated: A grand Himalayan pilgrimage honouring Goddess Nanda Devi, held once roughly every twelve years (with an annual fair in between).
howCelebrated: A four-horned ram leads a weeks-long trek through high mountains as devotees carry the goddess's palanquin to remote shrines.
imageQuery: Nanda Devi Raj Jat Uttarakhand Himalaya pilgrimage

title: Hornbill Festival
whyCelebrated: The 'Festival of Festivals' showcasing the cultures of all major Naga tribes, named after the revered hornbill bird.
howCelebrated: Held at Kisama Heritage Village near Kohima, it features tribal dances, music, indigenous games, crafts, food stalls and morungs of each tribe.
imageQuery: Hornbill Festival Nagaland tribal dance Kisama

title: Sekrenyi
whyCelebrated: A purification festival of the Angami Naga tribe, focused on cleansing body and soul and renewing community bonds.
howCelebrated: Ritual baths, traditional ceremonies, feasting and the singing of folk songs mark the multi-day celebration.

title: Yaoshang
whyCelebrated: Manipur's most important festival, coinciding with Holi, blending Vaishnav and indigenous Meitei traditions over five days.
howCelebrated: The highlight is Thabal Chongba, a moonlit folk dance where young people dance in circles; children collect donations, and sports events are held.

title: Ningol Chakouba
whyCelebrated: A Meitei festival celebrating the bond between married women (ningol) and their parental families.
howCelebrated: Married daughters are invited to their parental homes for a grand feast and given gifts, strengthening family ties.

title: Sangai Festival
whyCelebrated: Manipur's flagship tourism festival, named after the endangered Sangai (brow-antlered deer), showcasing the state's culture.
howCelebrated: The festival features indigenous dances, music, martial arts (Thang-Ta), crafts, cuisine and adventure activities across multiple venues.

title: Nongkrem Dance Festival
whyCelebrated: A five-day religious festival of the Khasi people, thanking God for a good harvest and praying for prosperity and peace.
howCelebrated: Held at Smit, it features the ceremonial Pomblang (goat sacrifice) and graceful dances by young men and women in traditional attire.

title: Wangala
whyCelebrated: The 'Hundred Drums' harvest festival of the Garo tribe, thanking Misi Saljong (the sun god) for a bountiful harvest.
howCelebrated: Warriors and dancers in feathered headgear perform to the rhythm of a hundred drums in colourful processions and dances.

title: Chapchar Kut
whyCelebrated: Mizoram's most important festival, a spring celebration held after the clearing of jungle for cultivation.
howCelebrated: Mizo people in traditional costumes perform the famed Cheraw (bamboo dance) and other folk dances to drums and gongs.

title: Mim Kut
whyCelebrated: A maize harvest festival of the Mizo people, also commemorating departed family members.
howCelebrated: Communities celebrate the harvest with feasting, rice beer, music and dance, and offer the season's produce in memory of the deceased.

title: Saga Dawa
whyCelebrated: The holiest Buddhist festival in Sikkim, marking the birth, enlightenment and parinirvana of Lord Buddha.
howCelebrated: Monks and devotees carry holy scriptures in processions, light butter lamps, and gather at monasteries for prayers and acts of merit.

title: Pang Lhabsol
whyCelebrated: A uniquely Sikkimese festival honouring Mount Khangchendzonga as the state's guardian deity.
howCelebrated: Monks perform the dramatic Pangtoed Cham warrior dance, and rituals reaffirm the historic bond between the Lepcha and Bhutia communities.
imageQuery: Pang Lhabsol Sikkim warrior dance monastery

title: Mopin Festival
whyCelebrated: A popular harvest festival of the Galo tribe of Arunachal Pradesh, invoking the goddess Mopin for prosperity and good harvest.
howCelebrated: People smear rice flour on each other, perform the graceful Popir dance, and share rice beer (apong) in community celebration.
imageQuery: Mopin Festival Arunachal Galo Popir dance

title: Ziro Festival of Music
whyCelebrated: An outdoor independent music festival set in the scenic Ziro valley, home of the Apatani tribe.
howCelebrated: Indie bands and artists from across India and abroad perform across open-air stages amid paddy fields and pine hills over four days.

title: Kharchi Puja
whyCelebrated: A festival worshipping fourteen deities of the Tripuri royal tradition, seeking cleansing of sin and prosperity for the land.
howCelebrated: The fourteen deities are bathed in the river and worshipped over a week; a large fair with folk performances accompanies the rituals.
imageQuery: Kharchi Puja Tripura fourteen deities fair

title: Garia Puja
whyCelebrated: A festival of Tripura's tribal communities worshipping Garia, the deity of livestock and wealth, for prosperity.
howCelebrated: A bamboo pole representing the deity is worshipped with offerings of fowl, rice beer and cotton, accompanied by the Garia dance.

title: Khajuraho Dance Festival
whyCelebrated: A week-long classical dance festival held against the backdrop of the UNESCO-listed Khajuraho temples.
howCelebrated: Renowned exponents of Kathak, Bharatanatyam, Odissi and other classical forms perform on open-air stages by the floodlit temples.
imageQuery: Khajuraho Dance Festival temple classical dance

title: Lokrang Festival
whyCelebrated: A cultural festival in Bhopal celebrating the folk and tribal arts of Madhya Pradesh and India.
howCelebrated: Folk dancers, musicians and artisans from various regions perform and exhibit crafts over several days of cultural programming.

title: Gugga Naumi
whyCelebrated: A folk festival of Haryana venerating Gugga Pir (Gugga Jaharveer), revered as a protector against snakes.
howCelebrated: Devotees take out processions with a decorated chhari (staff), sing folk ballads of Gugga, and offer prayers at his shrines.

title: Hemis Festival
whyCelebrated: A vibrant monastic festival at Hemis Monastery honouring Guru Padmasambhava (Guru Rinpoche), who brought Buddhism to the region.
howCelebrated: Lamas perform the masked Cham dance in elaborate brocade costumes to cymbals, drums and long horns, depicting the triumph of good over evil.
imageQuery: Hemis Festival Ladakh Cham masked dance

title: Ladakh Losar
whyCelebrated: The Ladakhi New Year, celebrated with rituals to drive away evil and welcome prosperity in the high Himalayan desert.
howCelebrated: Homes are decorated, ibex figures of dough are made, processions with fire and effigies are held, and families gather for prayers and feasts.

title: Masi Magam
whyCelebrated: A festival when deities from various temples are taken to the sea or rivers for a ritual holy bath, prominent in Puducherry.
howCelebrated: Idols are carried in procession to the seashore for a sacred immersion (theerthavari), with devotees taking dips and offering prayers.
imageQuery: Masi Magam Puducherry deity sea procession
